questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, what should a bus driver do with the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, put the bus in park. If the transmission has no park gear, put it in neutral instead.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be checked for all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, lug nuts must be present and tight. They must have no cracks, distortions, or rust. Check that bolt holes are also free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: What should the overhead inside mirror show?

options.text: The outside of the driver's side of the bus.
Students in the first four rows.

questions.explanation: The overhead inside mirror should let the driver see all students on the bus. This includes students sitting directly behind the driver.

questions.question: A post-trip inspection should include all of the following, except:

options.text: Looking for items left on the bus.

questions.explanation: After a trip, check for sleeping students, lost items, open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage or vandalism.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: Placing the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
The vehicle touching a boundary line.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of the vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides whether to proceed?

options.text: The vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver must decide whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: How should a driver complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull forward straight, then back to the left.
Back straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull forward straight, then back straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward straight, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. The vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Which maneuvers may be included in a basic vehicle control skills test?
questions.explanation: The test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What should the driver do while students load and unload the bus?
questions.explanation: Watch students as they enter and exit to prevent them from getting caught in doors or handrails. Make sure they move a safe distance away after exiting.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted on a school bus?
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before operating the bus.

questions.question: If your bus has a manual transmission, you should never ____ while crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Never shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Check that no trains are coming from any direction before you cross.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and move forward to get a better position. Just stopping without moving does not count as a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will be marked as errors.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, use it:
questions.explanation: Use a roof-mounted strobe light when visibility is poor, such as in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: At the first stoplight after you start your shift.

questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you start your trip.

questions.question: Before operating a school bus, ____ should be checked.
questions.explanation: Check all mirrors before driving. You need the best view possible. Have mirrors adjusted if needed to meet safety standards.

questions.question: When students load and unload a bus:

options.text: It is simple and does not need supervision.
It can be dangerous and needs supervision.
It can happen without the driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous and needs supervision.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Always follow safety rules and supervise this process.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, make sure:

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.explanation: Check the lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked securely.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: The header board must be secure, without damage, and strong enough to keep cargo in place.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at the bus stop assigned to them.
The driver should pick up students anywhere they are.
Parents can choose where the bus stop is located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at the bus stop assigned to them.
questions.explanation: Pick up and drop off students only at approved bus stops. The school district sets these stops.

questions.question: Bus stops can be changed by:
questions.explanation: The school district sets bus routes and stops. Never change a stop location without written approval from a district official.
